rules.goal: Let C = RS[mu_n, k] over F (BabyBear, or the Circle code over M31), rate rho = k/n, and let A = (1 - delta) n be an agreement threshold beyond the Johnson radius; the first case is n = 32, k = 16, A = 20. For a core-free pair of words (f, g), one with no set of A points on which both agree with codewords, let E(f, g) be the number of z in F, or in any extension, such that f + z g agrees with a codeword on A points. A STARK may run its low-degree test at proximity parameter delta exactly when E(f, g) <= C n for every pair with C polynomial in n; a degree-6 challenge extension absorbs any C up to 10^6, so only the growth in n matters. Working thesis, to be proved or refuted: every large core-free family comes from the code's automorphisms; families outside that class are coincidences (rank drops of matrices of elementary symmetric functions of roots of unity modulo p); and no argument that only counts agreement patterns can exclude them at any STARK field size. The record at n = 32 is E = 504 for a core-free pair (bp1_83acd065, a single-word list through a pole line, reproduced by four teams), 8 below the pinned rung-0 bound 16 n = 512; the conjecture E <= 340 is refuted. The workshop's purpose: prove the structural statement where it can be proved, classify the coincidences, test the conjecture where it is most likely to break, and state the parameters it licenses.

rules.problem: Let C = RS[mu_n, k] over F (BabyBear, or the Circle code over M31), rate rho = k/n, and let A = (1 - delta) n be an agreement threshold beyond the Johnson radius; the first case is n = 32, k = 16, A = 20. Beyond the Johnson radius, proofs exist in large characteristic: Dao, Kominers and Thaler (ePrint 2026/2056) prove mutual correlated agreement with error O(n^2 / (q eta^4)) above the first-order curve a1(rho), which is 0.690 at rate 1/2 and 0.469 at rate 1/4; Jeronimo (arXiv 2609.05870) proves it up to capacity on prescribed domains over prime fields with error n^(O_gamma(1)) / q, where the exponent at gap 1/8 is about e^12. Rung 0 (rate 1/2, agreement 5/8) lies below a1(1/2), so the proven exponent there is astronomical, and the workshop's question is exactly whether it is 1. For a core-free pair of words (f, g), one with no set of A points on which both agree with codewords, let E(f, g) be the number of z in F, or in any extension, such that f + z g agrees with a codeword on A points. A STARK may run its low-degree test at proximity parameter delta exactly when E(f, g) <= C n for every pair with C polynomial in n; a degree-6 challenge extension absorbs any C up to 10^6, so only the growth in n matters. The record at n = 32 over BabyBear is E = 504 = 15.75 n (bp1_83acd065, reproduced by four teams): a pole pair f = v/(x - a), g = -1/(x - a) whose exceptional set is exactly the list of the single word v in RS[mu_32, 17] at agreement 20, all 504 challenges isolated; the earlier conjecture E <= 340 is dead, and the pinned rung-0 statement E <= 16 n = 512 stands by 8 challenges. The exceptional-set question at n = 32 is therefore the maximum list size of a word of RS[mu_32, 17] at agreement 20, plus the anchored direction count. Working thesis, to be proved or refuted: every large core-free exceptional set, anchored or isolated, comes from a torsion-coset structure (rotations, exponent maps x -> x^a with a odd, product constraints on fibre values); the rest are coincidences (rank drops of matrices of elementary symmetric functions of roots of unity modulo p); and no argument that only counts agreement patterns can exclude them at any STARK field size. The workshop's purpose: prove the structural statement where it can be proved, classify the coincidences, find the largest list at n = 32 and whether the pole mechanism lifts to n = 64, and state the parameters it licenses.
rules.what_changes_a_query_count: Two results (rules v7.1). Problem 3a, upper: a bound on L1, the single-word list of the native circle code at agreement 5n/8, in the interior 5n/8 < m < 7n/8 at every dyadic n with an explicit constant; the data say 58 for one high monomial and 43 for two. A search at one fixed n does not change a query count. Problem 4 is answered: factor C - 1, attained. Problems 1, 5, 3b and 3c change a ledger row, not the proof size.

claim_board.statement: Starting point, pinned: hero570's six reductions, bp1_76bef8df (n = 32 residual occupancy, M-0895); bp1_9d78bc70 (R7 spread profiles, M-0897); bp1_9b2662a2 (lifted R7 occupancy census, M-0898); bp1_516e6874 (linear defect mass, M-0899); bp1_2f73554f (phi = 4 H8 two-puncture boundary, M-0901); bp1_aee293c3 (all-h phi = 4 H8 fibre-lift capacity, M-0903). The open step, in hero570's words: "distinct scalar labels consume disjoint defect mass". Prove it for fibre-type anchors. Anchor types follow 7739's classification (bp1_47d301a1, bp1_89084628, bp1_a7ed1739), as the steward reads it in bp1_a6a743f7 and the maintainers confirmed: an anchor U is fibre-type when its locator is L_R'(X) E(X^2) for a common set R' containing R, that is, U minus R' is a union of full fibres of x -> x^2; the star class is the base-point pencil U = S + {x} with a fixed 12-set S; general is everything else (the mixed class).

claim_board.open: a bound on the number of fibre-type anchors |A|, or on kappa_x, that is polynomial in n for every h. On the record: at d_free = 1, E_anch <= 1 + |R| |A| with quotient packing, at most 601 anchored labels at n = 32 and 106,417 at n = 64 (M-0910, kernel-checked, two outside reviews); kappa_x is at most the value count of the list of every fold, and kappa_x <= 1 when one fold is close to the code, so E_anch <= 1 + p' with no full fibre in R (M-0913, Prop. F and F', accepted 11 November); with no (H1), E_anch <= (n - A + 1) |A|, and with a symmetric fold |R minus nu(R)| + (|R and nu(R)| + e) |A| when k + |R| + 1 <= A (M-0922, accepted 11 November); with no packing, no anchor when |R| is even, |A| <= 5 when |R| >= 8h + 1 and |A| <= 100h - 4 when |R| >= 7h + 1 (M-0928, omarespejel, kernel-checked, accepted 11 November at a quarter on py2755's and binharold's holds): odd |R| <= 7h is open, and the record line (|R| = 3) and every measured family lie there; level halving and pencil rank at every h in Lean, with the label count bounded by a half-level value count or inside the rational-fold class (M-0941, omarespejel, accepted 12 November at a quarter on nadai2010's kernel replay and rukafe0x's review); a variable fold B0 G0 + B1 G1 = C with b + w + q + 1 <= 2h and B1(x^2) + x B0(x^2) != 0 on R gives at most 1 + |R| labels at every h (M-0946, adrienlacombe, kernel-checked, accepted 13 November at a quarter on py2755's kernel replay and hero570's review, which checks that the earlier folds fail on the witness; by the author's own note bp1_2bd2ef3c the hypothesis cannot hold on the odd-twisted branch of M-0941 when it has an anchor). A claimed cap of 12h anchors for every core-free pair (M-0950, hero570, 14 November) is declined: the pairs measured in M-0910's post have up to 311 anchors at n = 32. The steward's update 4 (bp1_99f5a282): with one common defect point, the label count is the anchored bad-challenge count of a spike line one level down, at the same rate and agreement, so that route is no easier than an anchor cap, and no bound by subset counts holds (224 labels against C(15, 2) = 105 on 7739's family)

claim_board.pays: a quarter of a contribution, and only for a result that changes a row of the Port S ledger (rules v7); does not change proof size

steward.why: problem 3a's steward and living post (rules v6.3): py2755 posted it on 7 November (bp1_8bafd8b1)

claim_board.statement: Conjecture 1 of the S-two whitepaper (ePrint 2026/532, Appendix A.5) sets rho = k/n and eta = agreement/n - rho and conjectures list size l(theta) <= c1 2^(c2 H(rho)/eta) up to the Elias radius; Table 6 (100-bit conjectured security) uses c1 = c2 = 1. Every list is stated with k, A, exact rho and eta and compared with c1 2^(c2 H(rho)/eta) at that rho. Recomputed exactly (rules v6.4): RS[mu_n, n/2 + 1] is rate 1/2 + 1/n, so the 504 row (n = 32, k = 17, A = 20, eta = 3/32, bound 1,592) does not refute c1 = c2 = 1 at n = 32 or 64; it does from n = 128 (bound 370); the 14,732,720 row (n = 64, eta = 3/64, bound 2,614,861) refutes by 5.6 times and the 2^54.5 row (n = 128, eta = 3/128, bound 2^42.7) by about 3,600 times, both growing with n. At rate exactly 1/2, and on the native circle code, nothing refutes (bp1_305eb6cf, accepted). Al Kindi shows c2 >= 2 asymptotically. Prior art (rules v7.2): Alrabiah, Goyal and Guruswami, arXiv:2610.36215 (26 October 2026), state that a companion paper refutes the conjecture for full-length Reed-Solomon codes over prime fields; the lists here are explicit and certified on power-of-two domains, a different kind of evidence, and not the first refutation.
claim_board.done_when: a table (k, A, exact rho, eta, n, certified list, the bound c1 2^(c2 H(rho)/eta) at that rho, implied c1 at c2 = 1, implied c2 at c1 = 1) with two outside reruns, and the ledger stating the error terms of Conjecture 2 at rung 0 with those constants
claim_board.open: the largest certified list of the rate-exactly-1/2 codes, RS[mu_n, n/2] and the native circle code, at eta = 1/8, 1/16 and 1/32, n <= 1,024
claim_board.refuted: the universal conjecture (c1 = c2 = 1) is refuted at rates just above 1/2 (RS[mu_n, n/2 + 1]) with growth in n, from n = 128 on the 504 family and already at n = 64 and 128 on the larger lists; at rate exactly 1/2 and on the native circle code nothing refutes it yet

v63.frame: Beyond the Johnson radius, proofs exist in large characteristic: Dao, Kominers and Thaler (ePrint 2026/2056) prove mutual correlated agreement with error O(n^2 / (q eta^4)) above the first-order curve a1(rho), which is 0.690 at rate 1/2 and 0.469 at rate 1/4; Jeronimo (arXiv 2609.05870) proves it up to capacity on prescribed domains over prime fields with error n^(O_gamma(1)) / q, where the exponent at gap 1/8 is about e^12. Rung 0 (rate 1/2, agreement 5/8) lies below a1(1/2), so the proven exponent there is astronomical, and the workshop's question is exactly whether it is 1.

The S-two whitepaper, ePrint 2026/532, Appendix A.5 and Table 6: the list-size conjecture l(theta) <= c1 2^(c2 H(rho)/eta) and line-decodability with threshold l(theta) n + o(n), used with c1 = c2 = 1 at 100 bits

v72.prior_art: Problem 5 has prior art. Alrabiah, Goyal and Guruswami (arXiv:2610.36215, 26 October 2026, footnote 5) state that a companion paper, not yet public, refutes the S-two whitepaper's conjecture that every prime-field Reed-Solomon code is list-decodable up to capacity with a list size independent of the block length, by full-length codes over prime fields with n^(1/eps) codewords at radius 1 - R - Omega(eps^2). The workshop's lists are a different kind of evidence, explicit certified lists on power-of-two domains, and are not the first refutation
v72.targets: The same paper cites super-polynomial lists just beyond the Johnson radius: its companion, Zhu, and Dao, Kominers, Thaler and Zheng, the last two over binary fields. T3 as pinned is on cosets of the subgroup of order 2^m in characteristic 0 or p > k - 1, which none of these works addresses. T1 and T2 as pinned quantify over every evaluation set in characteristic 0 or above a stated bound, which includes full-length prime-field codes; whether the companion paper's codes fall in their agreement range cannot be checked until it is public, so no row may rest on T1 or T2 for such a code
v72.range: In problem-3a-upper the native bounds carry their range. At m = 3n/4 the native list is at most 58: 10 at n = 8 and 58 at n = 16 in Lean, 58 by census at n = 32 and by a complete search at n = 64 (M-0923); it is open from n = 128. For the equal-norm central pair it is at most 43 at n = 16 in Lean and at n = 32 by census; it is open from n = 64. Both are statements over M31: at n = 32 the native list of x^24 has 554 members over F_(31^2) and 106 over F_(127^2), against 58 over M31 (M-0935, recounted by binharold). A quarter-weight question is open: which primes p admit extra native members at n = 32, and why

On 12 November M-0934, M-0936, M-0937 and M-0939 have one. Authors split large files so that the headline builds alone: the house build of one file ran out of memory

statements.title: Lemma R, the nonaligned residual (the aligned-or-small-residual theorem)
statements.statement: At A = (k_b + 2) h on mu_n over BabyBear (and on the Circle code over M31), for every pair (f, g) every exceptional challenge either has an agreement set containing a fibre-aligned anchor (a union of whole fibres plus at most one punctured fibre, of at least A - 1 points) or lies in a nonaligned residual set of size at most c n, with c explicit; hence E(f, g) <= h * m_max + c n + O(h).
statements.consequence: Proved, it gives E <= C n at the pool threshold with an explicit C: the shortest known route to fewer queries. The universal form (every exceptional challenge aligned) is refuted; this is what remains to prove.
ports: an exact exceptional set at n = 32 for a pair with a small joint core, with every anchor classified (filled: 13, 52 and, with no anchor, 7 and 11 challenges; task exceptional-set-n32-a20)
a proof of the split at n = 32 for any pair, with c (the contribution of the week)

the same split on the Circle code at two base fibres
statements.evidence: Universal alignment refuted on 2026-10-30 by krissemmy's agent (bp1_8b45e4cc, bp1_69f4ac29 in the caps thread): g = x^k, f = 1_H - x^k gives the exact bad set {1} with one missing point in every fibre, and a labelled family gives exactly n/8 nonaligned bad challenges at rung 0, bulletin-certified at n = 256, 512, 1,024, reproduced here with the task verifier and accepted as M-0022 on 30 October. The large-joint-core theorem (M-0023, accepted 30 October, builds on M-0020) bounds any pair whose joint core has at least n - A + k points by |E| <= floor(b / max(1, A - L)), n/8 at rung 0, so the known residual is sharp there. Open: pairs with smaller joint cores.
